title: Five A.M.
logline: Five in the morning, a silent kitchen, the first quiet minutes before a long study session. Every sound of the ritual with {{product.name}}, heard up close.

ingested: seal, pour, ice and texture are the most proven ASMR triggers
applied: caps, pumps and textures spreading on skin are native to the genre
worn: zips, clasps and fabric brush are strong; footwear loses the lips-and-chin payoff and cuts to the floor
handheld: clicks, snaps and power-on tones carry the film
carried: zip purrs and leather creak are rich; the payoff is quieter
home: countertop pieces (lamps, candles, kettles, bedding, diffusers) are ideal; large furniture sits under the window and shows only in macro
consumable: seal tears and refill clicks; the use moment depends on the product having a satisfying mechanism

avoid: sleep aids or sedatives (the ritual starts a study session)
silent products with no tactile or audible character (the genre depends on the product's own sounds)
anything used on intimate areas of the body

lore: Imani Brooks is a second-year public health grad student renting the top floor of a 1920s brick row house in West Philadelphia. Her qualifying exam is in six days.

The counter is a salvaged walnut slab from a closed neighbourhood bakery, topped with a honed black slate board; she oils the walnut every Sunday and the slate still carries a pale water ring from the first week.

She has kept the same ritual for 41 mornings in a row: 5am, the one product she always reaches for, one page of pencil notes before the sun comes up. The notebook is the fifth Aldercroft notebook this semester.
The basalt ice bowl was her grandmother's; it is rough and pitted outside and polished smooth inside from decades of use.
The radiator knocks twice at 5:03 every morning; that is her cue to begin.

every product sound comes from sound_by_archetype below: the product's own tactile sounds are the score

sound_by_archetype._rule: Sound is the product. Each archetype has its own chain of close-mic, dry, native sounds, one per shot, all made by the product itself or the hand on it. The hero sound (S05) always has half a second of silence before it. Never borrow a sound the product cannot make; if the product is quieter than listed, pick its real quietest sound and let the room tone carry it.

beats.summary: Silence, then a fingertip drags slowly across the product's surface and we hear it. A whisper: listen.
The ritual: one small prep gesture, the product settled in its place, two soft taps.
The hero sound: a nail at the opening point, half a second of silence, the product opens or switches on, its texture up close.
The use moment in slow motion and its aftermath settling.
Her quiet moment with the product, a soft exhale, the brand whispered; then the pencil starts scratching: the study session begins.
The product alone on the slate, one last small sound; the tagline whispered.
